near_miss.lead: ON 'at miðri nótt er menn váro í svefni' / 'um nóttina er menn váro sofnaðir' ~ Hdt 'πρόσω τῆς νυκτὸς ... ἄνθρωποι εἶναι ἐν ὕπνῳ' (*h1es- + *en + *swepno-/supno-, time-setting for a covert move by night); cf. MBh 1.100.8 'supta jana prāye niśīthe'
near_miss.why_not: Cognate 'be in sleep' with night in congruent contexts (stealthy action timed while men sleep) in ON, Greek and Sanskrit epic, but the search shows sleep+night is everyday saga prose (97 Germanic, 126 Greek hits within 6 words); a natural narrative topos, not distinctive enough to claim as inherited.

near_miss.lead: ON 'at miðri nótt' ~ Gk 'νύκτα μέσην' ~ Lat 'media nocte' (Pl. Amph. 514): *médʰyā nókʷts 'midnight'
near_miss.why_not: Exact cognate adj+noun time expression in Gmc, Gk, Lat (Sanskrit renews it: ardharātra, niśītha), but a compositional time phrase that each language could form on its own; a lexical collocation, not phraseology I would defend as inherited.

near_miss.lead: ON 'lágu ... þar um nóttina' / 'lágo þar um nótt' ~ ORV 'въ ту нощь лежащю' (*legʰ- + *nokʷt-, 'lie (somewhere) that night')
near_miss.why_not: Cognate verb and noun, but the ON is nautical ('lay at anchor'), the ORV a guest staying at a courtyard; 'stay/lie overnight' is generic.

near_miss.lead: Genealogical apposition 'daughter of X and sister of Y' (ON 'dóttor Sveins konongs en systor Knúts' ~ AV 'śraddhāyā duhitā ... svasā ṛṣīṇām')
near_miss.why_not: Cognate kin terms *dʰugh2tēr/*swesōr in apposition, but genealogical listing is generic and the AV is a personified girdle, not a dynastic record.

near_miss.lead: ON alliterative binomial 'líf eða limar' / 'lífi oc límum' ('life and limb')
near_miss.why_not: A real Germanic legal binomial (cf. later English 'life and limb'), but the Greek partner shares only mapped roots (λιποῦσα, ὠλένας), with no cognate pair or parallel; no cross-branch match.

near_miss.lead: ON 'bar Karl orð oc jartegnir' ~ Hdt 'τὰς ἀγγελίας φέρειν' (*bʰer- + message, a king's messenger)
near_miss.why_not: Only the verb is cognate (the noun is renewed); 'carry a message' is universal.

near_miss.lead: ON 'þing var sett þa stoð konongr up oc mælti' (rising to speak in an assembly), cf. Homeric 'ἀνστὰς ... μετέφη'
near_miss.why_not: The Greek slab partners have no such scene; the Homeric parallel is an outside recollection, and rising to speak is generic narrative.

near_miss.lead: ON 'orðom ... qvað af tungo fram' ~ Lucr. 'uerborum daedala lingua' (*werdʰo- + *dn̥ǵʰweh2- 'tongue', speech production)
near_miss.why_not: Both pairs are cognate, but 'words and tongue' is physiologically trivial; the contexts differ (the ON praises a skald's fluency, Lucretius gives a physics of the voice).

near_miss.lead: ON 'fell hann til fóta ... lagði insiglit i kne honom' (laying a thing on the knees of a superior), cf. Homeric 'θεῶν ἐν γούνασι κεῖται'
near_miss.why_not: The Greek partners use γούνατα in unrelated senses (knees of a dead man, 'loosened the knees'); the knee-supplication link is my own outside association with no slab support.

near_miss.lead: ON 'orti flocc' (yrkja = to compose verse, *werǵ-) beside Gk 'μέγα ἔργον ἔρδειν'
near_miss.why_not: The Greek is a figura 'do a great deed', the ON a verb of poetic composition; there is no shared collocation.

near_miss.lead: Name-asking / 'hear my words' (ON 'nafn mitt ... ec em callaðr' ~ Eur. 'τίς ὀνομάζεται'; 'heyri ec orð þin' ~ 'nolunt audire')
near_miss.why_not: Generic dialogue; there are no cognate collocations beyond *h1nomn̥ and *h2ḱh2ows-.

near_miss.lead: Sleep/meal sequence, 'went to sleep', kin terms, 'bind a treaty with oaths' (ON 'sáttmál svardǫgum binda'), skaldic battle stanza against Irish saga
near_miss.why_not: The partners show no congruent phrase; these are shared roots only.

search_lead.cognate: ON varmr ~ Gk θερμός only if Gmc *warma- continues *gʷʰormo- (disputed); blood words renewed (blóð vs αἷμα)
search_lead.argument: Sigvatr's 'bloð com varmt' (warm blood flowed in battle) matches the Homeric 'αἷμ̓ ἔτι θερμόν' welling from a wound. The motif is natural and the cognacy doubtful, so this is a weak lead only.

error.correct_reading: varmr 'warm', not from the 'worm' word *wr̥mi-; usually *gʷʰormo- (θερμός) or *wer- 'burn'
njóta, pret. 3sg naut 'enjoyed, benefited from' (+gen. drotningar)
error.evidence: 'naut hann drotningar at því er hann helt lífi' = 'he owed it to the queen that he kept his life'; not naut 'cattle'
'er konongr hætti rǫþo sinni' = 'when the king ended his speech'

error.correct_reading: maðr, acc. sg. man(n), in 'þan micla man nefndan Arnliot'
error.evidence: an adjective plus a participle agree with an acc. masc. noun 'man'

error.correct_reading: proper name Karl (Karl mœrski, 'møogon;rski' in the OCR)
error.evidence: 'ec em callaðr Karl møogon;rski'; also Karl/Karli in AM-36-fol 364:01 (w2/8)

proper name Sveinn (Sveinn Úlfsson, later king of Denmark)
